notespost: Day twenty two on eight hundred calories a day. If this continues, I can sense a certain loss of internal balance beginning to emerge. At the same time, it is interesting to observe how the mind begins to attach itself to unexpected patterns, especially in moments when physical and mental states are pushed beyond their usual limits.

A brief summary of what has been occupying my mind lately. I recently came across Girlhood’s song 'buligyilkos', and while listening to it I found myself reflecting on a broader idea. It made me think about how artists who grow up within a similar cultural and musical environment often develop an unspoken connection. When the same international influences shape different individuals at a similar stage of life, a certain shared language emerges between them. I often sense this kind of alignment with artists from my own generation.

I would also like to briefly mention the producer behind this track. In my view, his work stands out within the current Hungarian music scene for its clarity and distinct character. There are moments in the arrangement that echo familiar motifs, such as elements reminiscent of 'közöny', yet they are placed in a way that still feels intentional within the context of the piece. More broadly, I find it compelling when an artist’s sound remains recognisable while still capable of evoking a genuine emotional response through both voice and lyrical tone.

Beyond this, I have been increasingly drawn to the idea of how the perception of time reshapes the way experiences are valued. As circumstances change, certain moments begin to carry a different weight, often appearing more meaningful when viewed from a distance. The awareness that everything is finite seems to deepen this effect, placing even ordinary experiences into a more considered perspective.

At the same time, there is a transitional phase I am currently moving through. The direction of my work has become more defined, both in terms of sound and structure, yet the process itself requires a level of discipline that is not always easy to sustain. It creates a certain tension between where I am and where I intend to arrive. However, this tension also serves as a necessary part of the process, gradually shaping the conditions in which the next phase of my work can exist.

What matters is that the direction itself is clear. The intention remains to build a space where music, visuals, and ideas can come together as a unified expression. The process may be gradual, but it is already in motion, and that alone gives it purpose.

I decided to start using this page for what it was originally meant to be, as a place to document thoughts. Since most of my communication will exist through music and visuals, this space serves as a quieter layer behind it, for those who are interested in what lies beneath the sound.

I have been thinking about how a person’s core musical taste seems to form around the age of fifteen or sixteen. The emotional state one inhabits during that time, along with the music that accompanies it, appears to leave a lasting imprint that follows throughout life, whether consciously or not. There is also a strong connection between early emotional experiences and the music associated with them. Music, in this sense, functions almost like a time capsule, capable of bringing back entire states of mind with remarkable clarity.

What I find increasingly interesting is how the perception of experiences changes over time. Moments that once carried a certain weight and rarity can gradually lose their significance as life circumstances shift and access to those same experiences becomes easier. This raises a question: do these moments truly lose their value, or is it simply that their uniqueness can only ever be fully felt the first time they are lived. It may be that the mind is wired in such a way that repetition diminishes intensity, leaving only the memory of what once felt irreplaceable.

Over time, perspective also changes. Certain qualities that once felt incompatible can later become essential. It becomes clear that a deep level of understanding between individuals often depends on a shared intensity toward something meaningful. Without that, it is difficult to bridge the gap between inner worlds. In my case, that reference point has always been music.
